Set {{liveSecretKey}} to an sk_live_ key and {{consoleAdminToken}} to a console JWT with the tenant_admin role for the environment-scoped requests.

request.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe. Returns engine process status and system timestamp without pinging database/cache dependencies.

item.name: Sign Up — 400 Weak Password Policy Rejection

request.description:
Malformed address rejected by format validation before any user lookup, so this 400 is distinguishable from the enumeration-safe 200 above.

Response (400): code=validation_failed, "invalid email address format" (internal/auth/auth_handlers.go ResendVerification).

Native/mobile login: refresh token delivered directly in JSON body.

Verified response (200):
{
  "user": {...},
  "access_token": "...",
  "refresh_token": "c9a9df1fe74055eea42a8711d1725858..."
}

User has active TOTP 2FA. Access token is withheld until second factor verification.

Verified response (200):
{
  "user": {...},
  "mfa_required": true,
  "mfa_token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "methods": ["totp"]
}

Verified response (401):
{"error":"missing publishable API key in X-Authn-Publishable-Key header"}

With Redis unreachable the limiter refuses the request instead of admitting it: an outage must not become an unlimited-credential-stuffing window.

Response (503): code=service_unavailable, "rate limit service unavailable" (internal/ratelimit/limiter.go:413). Distinguish from 429, which means a real budget was exceeded.

Rotate valid refresh token for new access_token JWT + newly rotated refresh_token.

Verified response (200):
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "refresh_token": "512bbc00-1004-4607...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 900,
  "session_id": "ses_1e12795c-48f"
}

Replaying recently rotated refresh token within 10s grace window returns current active tokens without re-rotating (prevents tab race condition token loss).

Verified response (200):
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGci...",
  "refresh_token": "",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 900,
  "session_id": "ses_1e12795c-48f"
}

Initiates OAuth authorization flow, generates 32-byte CSRF state token in Redis (10m TTL), and returns 302 Redirect to provider.

Verified response (302 Found):
Location: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?access_type=offline&client_id=...&state=bceb5c5bb75bea309b1aff15df6195a5
Handles provider OAuth authorization code callback. Consumes single-use CSRF state token and exchanges code for user profile and JWT access token.

Creates a new custom RBAC role with validated permission syntax.

Verified response (201 Created):
{
  "id": "rol_a87d51ff-021",
  "name": "Content Manager",
  "slug": "content_manager"
}
Lists all roles and permissions configured for the tenant.

Evaluates active user's roles and permissions.

Verified response (200):
{
  "user_id": "usr_vanilla_007",
  "roles": ["content_manager"],
  "permissions": ["posts:create", "posts:delete", "posts:read", "posts:update"]
}

Initiates account recovery. Performs timing-safe Argon2id hash for non-existent users.

item.name: Account Recovery — Cancel via Token (Security Cancellation)

request.description: Owner cancels fraudulent recovery request. Immediately terminates request and blacklists attacker IP/subnet in Redis for 7 days (403 Forbidden).

Creates a new B2B Organization workspace in the environment of the presented key. The slug is unique per tenant and environment, so the same slug is claimable once in test and once in live, and a workspace is visible only to keys in its own environment.

Verified response (201 Created):
{
  "id": "org_9038723e-062",
  "environment": "test",
  "name": "Acme Corporation",
  "slug": "acme-corp-101"
}

A test key past TEST_MAX_ORGANIZATIONS answers 403 test_quota_exceeded.
Creates a 32-byte cryptographic team member invitation.
Accepts team invitation token. Single-use enforcement prevents token replay attacks.
Retrieves tenant impersonation guardrail policy configuration.
Lists all active and revoked API keys for the caller's application. Never exposes raw keys or hashes.
Shallow engine liveness probe. Returns 200 OK and timestamp.
Deep readiness probe. Verifies database and Redis connectivity.

Dispatches a test ping event signed with HMAC SHA-256 (X-Authn-Signature). A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.

Rotates HMAC signing secret for an endpoint. A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.
Standard OIDC UserInfo endpoint returning sub, email, email_verified, name, tenant_id, environment, updated_at.
Fetches authenticated user profile, phone, recovery email status, avatar, locale, and metadata.
Registers a secondary backup recovery email address and dispatches a single-use verification token link.
Inspects email domain to check if active SAML SSO exists and if enforce_sso is enabled prior to login.

Creates SAML 2.0 IdP configuration for an organization (admin secret key required). environment is test here so the request runs against the demo credentials. A connection in live is what an organization's real employees sign in through, so naming live — or omitting the field, whose default is live — takes a live key and is otherwise refused 403 live_key_required.
Sends a single-use 15-min magic link to user's email. Auto-provisions new account if user doesn't exist.

POST only. The emailed link opens the application's own frontend, which posts the token here with its publishable key as a header. There is no GET form: a GET would answer a top-level browser navigation with an access token in the body, which the browser records in history and leaks as a Referer.
Returns QR code URI and secret. Status goes to pending.
Validates initial TOTP code. Transitions status pending → active.
Issues 8 new single-use XXXX-XXXX codes. Previous codes invalidated immediately.

The login-path SMS send. Authorized by the mfa_token from POST /v1/client/auth/login rather than by a session, so there is no Authorization header.

Do not confuse it with Enroll: enroll adds a new number and needs a session, while this delivers a code to the number already confirmed on the account. Verification reads the code from server memory and a code exists only once it has been sent, so on the login path this request is what creates one.

Requires `sms` in the token's sealed `methods`, delivers only to an enabled number, and has no email fallback: this caller has proven the password alone, so mailing the second factor to the account address would reduce two factors to one. Budget is 3 sends per 10 minutes per user.

Verified response (200):
{
  "message": "Verification code sent via SMS",
  "phone_number": "+12•••99",
  "expires_in_seconds": 300
}

Then submit the delivered code to "Verify 2FA Challenge" with "method": "sms".

A token that does not verify answers 401 invalid_token. For contrast: a challenge whose `methods` omit sms answers 400 validation_failed, an account with no confirmed number answers 400 not_found, and a spent send budget answers 429 rate_limited.
Edge case: cannot delete last active 2FA method if no password auth.
Pre-enroll 1-5 guardians. Generates GF(2^8) Shamir shares. Raw shares delivered ONLY in guardian email URL fragment. DB stores SHA-256 hashes only.
Revokes guardian and triggers Re-Key/Re-Split of all Shamir shares.
Unauthenticated. Resolves available proof methods in priority order. Non-existent email returns timing-safe generic response (anti-enumeration).
Same request from a blacklisted IP should return 403 ErrOriginBlacklisted.
Submit k-of-N Shamir share. Threshold met when k valid shares submitted.
Only available when trusted device token + familiar subnet confirmed by Telemetry Engine.
15-min single-use claim token. Resets password with Argon2id, wipes 2FA, issues 8 fresh recovery codes, revokes old sessions.
Cancels recovery, creates 7-day blacklist, flags security_review_required=true. Preserves cancelling session.
Public unauthenticated. Token from security alert email URL fragment. Revokes ALL active user sessions.
Exact-match redirect_uri validation. Must fail for non-whitelisted URI.
freeze_window_hours=5 violates min 24. All methods disabled violates rule 7.

Cookie SameSite plus access and refresh token lifetimes for the environment the key belongs to. A zero lifetime means the environment inherits the deployment default, not that sessions expire instantly.

access_token_ttl_minutes is a fixed menu — 15, 30 or 60, or 0 to inherit the deployment default — and an unlisted value is refused with 422 validation_failed. Try 45 to see it. The refresh lifetime is still clamped into its window and an unrecognised cookie_same_site still becomes lax, so read the response rather than assuming the request applied verbatim.

Every policy column of the key's environment in one read. Social provider client secrets come back as a client_secret_set boolean. An empty column means nothing is configured there and the engine defaults apply — it is not everything switched off.

Answers what will change in live if test is published. Both environments come back whichever key is used, since comparing them is the point. Read this before publishing — it catches the branding edit you made in test three weeks ago and forgot about.

Copies all seven policy columns from test onto live and stamps published_at. The body may be omitted entirely — test to live is the default.

The copy is wholesale, not selective, so publishing an empty test environment clears live. That is the faithful meaning of make-live-match-test, which is why the diff request above exists.

Needs a live key: set liveSecretKey to one. changed lists the columns that actually moved, measured before the write.

item.name: Publish Into Live With A Test Key (expect 403)

request.description: The destination must be the key's own environment. Without this guard a test key could overwrite a live configuration, which is the one thing the environment split exists to prevent. Expect 403 'publishing into live requires a live secret key'.

Refused rather than treated as a no-op. It would report success while stamping published_at, making the audit trail claim a promotion that never happened. Expect 400 'from and to must name different environments'.

Registers a new outgoing webhook endpoint and generates an encrypted HMAC signing secret. A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.

item.name: Register Webhook Endpoint With A Test Key (expect 403)

request.description:
The same request as above with the test key, refused rather than filed. There is one endpoint list per tenant and the dispatcher delivers every event to all of it, so an entry a test key added would receive live traffic.

Expect 403 with code live_key_required and a message naming the credential rather than a permission — the operator being refused usually holds the live key already and reached for the wrong one.
Lists all registered webhook endpoints for tenant. Readable with either key: seeing the other environment's configuration crosses nothing, changing it does.
Fetches a specific webhook endpoint by ID. Readable with either key: seeing the other environment's configuration crosses nothing, changing it does.

Dispatches an immediate test ping event to verify HMAC signature processing. A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.

Rotates endpoint HMAC signing secret key. A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.

Deletes webhook endpoint and cascade deletes associated child delivery logs. A webhook endpoint has no environment of its own: one list per tenant, delivered to in full. Writing it therefore takes a live key — set liveSecretKey to one. A test key is refused 403 live_key_required.
Retrieves tenant impersonation policy rules and maximum duration caps.
Configures tenant impersonation boundaries and mandatory step-up auth requirements.
Verifies 400 Bad Request error when admin step-up auth (password/2FA) is omitted.
Executes admin impersonation with mandatory step-up password verification and issues a short-lived Impersonation JWT.
Verifies that destructive account mutations (password reset) are blocked with 403 Forbidden during active impersonation.
Exits the active impersonation session and invalidates the session context.

The one call a sign-in page makes before it renders: branding, the sign-in and second-factor methods to offer, the effective password rules, the email verification mode, and the enabled recovery methods. Tenant, application and environment come from the publishable key, so there is no body and no query parameter. Withheld by design: recovery thresholds, provider credentials, and the CORS and redirect allowlists.
Reads the stored branding behind the bootstrap document. The tenant is taken from the credential, so no target may be named.

Replaces the tenant's branding wholesale — a merge would make clearing a logo impossible. Every field may be empty. Colours must be hex, URLs must be http(s), and a value that could escape a CSS declaration or the enclosing <style> element is refused with 400 naming the field, since branding renders on the page where a user types their password. A publishable key is refused here.

Negative case. The payload closes the <style> element the stylesheet is delivered in and would execute on every sign-in page the tenant serves. Expect 400 with code validation_failed, naming custom_css.

Creates a new B2B Organization workspace and auto-assigns creator as org_admin. The workspace lands in the environment of the presented key and the response echoes it; a test key past TEST_MAX_ORGANIZATIONS answers 403 test_quota_exceeded.
Lists all organizations accessible to the caller.
Fetches organization details by ID.
Lists all members of an organization with role assignments.
Generates a 32-byte cryptographically random single-use invitation token with 7-day expiry.
Redeems invitation token, adds user to organization with assigned role, and updates token status to accepted.

Configures SAML 2.0 Identity Provider settings and domain SSO enforcement for an organization. environment is test here so the request runs against the demo credentials. A connection in live is what an organization's real employees sign in through, so naming live — or omitting the field, whose default is live — takes a live key and is otherwise refused 403 live_key_required.
Inspects email domain to check if active SAML SSO exists and whether enforce_sso is enabled.
Generates Service Provider XML metadata document for Okta / Azure AD import.

Assertion Consumer Service. Unauthenticated by protocol necessity — the identity provider holds no Authn key — so no publishable key is sent; the tenant is derived from the assertion Issuer and the protection is XML signature validation.

Set samlRelayState to a URL registered in exact_redirect_uris on one of the tenant's applications. The response is 302 with the access token in the Location fragment and the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie.

Turn OFF 'Automatically follow redirects' in Postman settings, or Postman will follow the Location and show you the landing page instead of the header you are trying to inspect.

Note that an assertion is single-use: replaying the same samlResponseBase64 returns 403.

Same assertion, with a RelayState the tenant never registered. Anyone can craft a link to an identity provider's SSO URL carrying any RelayState, and the provider echoes it back here — so an unchecked value would hand a real employee's access token to whoever chose the URL.

Expect 200 with the token in the body and NO Location header. The sign-in still succeeds: the assertion has already been consumed and is single-use, so refusing would cost the user an authentication they cannot retry. The refusal is logged server-side as '[SAML] relay state refused for tenant ...'.

Every email and SMS the test environment produced, newest first, instead of sending them. Interception happens at the provider interface, so all seven send sites — signup verification, password reset, magic link, email-change confirmation, OTP, MFA codes and invitations — land here without any of them knowing.

The listing omits the rendered body but keeps the fields a harness reads: 'code' carries the extracted one-time code and 'metadata.link' the action URL, both pulled out at capture time.

Verified response (200):
{"environment":"test","total":1,"messages":[{"id":"sbm_...","channel":"email","environment":"test","recipient":"user@example.com","subject":"Verify your email","template":"email_verification","metadata":{"link":"http://localhost:3000/verify?token=..."},"created_at":"2026-08-19T10:00:00Z"}]}

Narrows the inbox to one recipient and channel, which is how a test finds its own message when a suite runs several flows against the same tenant. 'total' is the count matching the filter rather than the page size, so a harness can tell 'my message has not arrived yet' from 'I am looking at the wrong page'.

'channel' accepts only 'email' or 'sms'; anything else is 400 with code VALIDATION_FAILED. 'limit' and 'offset' must parse as integers.

Reads one capture including 'body', the fully rendered document — the only place it is returned, because a listing carrying every rendered template would be tens of times larger than the fields anyone pages through it for.

Set {{sandboxMessageId}} from an 'id' in the listing above. An id belonging to another tenant is 404, not 403: the store is scoped to the calling tenant, so an unknown id and somebody else's id are indistinguishable from inside, and answering 403 would confirm the row exists.

Deletes the calling tenant's captures and reports how many went. Run it between suites so a test can assert on 'the newest message' without the previous run's captures standing in front of it.

Captures also expire on their own: the retention sweeper removes anything older than SANDBOX_MESSAGE_RETENTION (24h by default), because these bodies hold working verification links and one-time codes in plain text.

Verified response (200):
{"message":"sandbox inbox emptied","environment":"test","removed":3}

item.name: List Captured Messages With A Live Key (expect 403)

request.description:
A live credential is refused rather than answered with an empty list. Nothing is ever captured outside test, so an empty list would be a true answer to the wrong question, and 'my message is missing' is a far worse conclusion to leave an operator with than 'you are looking at the wrong environment'.

Expect 403 with code FORBIDDEN and a message naming the environment the credential addresses. Requires {{liveSecretKey}} to be set to an sk_live_ key.

item.name: Verify Email Delivery Through The Configured Provider

request.description:
Sends one real message through the configured provider, deliberately bypassing the sandbox. That bypass is the entire point: a captured message never reaches a provider, so no amount of sandbox traffic establishes that the SMTP or API credentials in configuration actually work. Sending is the only test of a send.

There is no recipient field. The address is the signed-in operator's own, which makes it impossible to aim the endpoint at somebody else rather than merely against the rules. An operator whose own email is unverified is refused with 403 EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED before anything is sent.

{{consoleAdminToken}} must be a console JWT carrying the tenant_admin role. The response names the driver that answered, so the result cannot be misread as coming from a backend you are not looking at.

Verified response (200):
{"message":"delivery test accepted by the provider","channel":"email","recipient":"admin@example.com","driver":"smtp"}

A provider that rejects the message is 502; no provider configured at all is 503.

item.name: Verify SMS Delivery Through The Configured Provider

request.description:
The SMS half of the same check, sent to the operator's own verified phone number. An account with no phone number, or one that is present but unverified, is 403 — an unverified number is somebody else's until it is proven, and text messages cost money to strangers.

Both channels share a cap of three verifications per tenant per rate-limit window; a fourth is 429 with Retry-After in seconds. The provider's answer does not change between attempts, so repeating the call only spends quota.

item.name: Verify Delivery With A Secret Key (expect 403)

request.description:
A secret key authenticates the endpoint but cannot use it. The key identifies an application rather than a person, so there is no address behind it that the engine has watched anybody prove control of — and requiring the console credential is what keeps the recipient something the engine already knows instead of something the caller supplies.

Expect 403 with code FORBIDDEN. This is the mirror image of the inbox: the inbox is test-only and takes a secret key, delivery verification is console-only and works in either environment.

item.name: Verify Delivery With An Unknown Channel (expect 400)

request.description:
The channel is validated before the operator is looked up or any quota is spent, so a typo costs nothing and leaks nothing about the account.

Expect 400 with code VALIDATION_FAILED and the message "channel must be 'email' or 'sms'".
